s1.syndrome_frame: Severe respiratory infection with subsequent ocular involvement
salient_findings: Blurred vision and redness in one eye
Relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma
key_facts: Woman in her late 50s hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia
Recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history reported
Developed blurred vision and redness in one eye on day 2 post-admission
Temporary pain when mobilizing the globe
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD and 0 logMAR OS
Relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and impaired color and contrast vision in the right eye
Mild anterior chamber inflammation and noticeable pupillary edema
Normal complete blood cell counts and serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels
Negative results for syphilis, HIV, Toxoplasma gondii, and Borrelia serologies
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Normal cranial MRI with fine optic nerve cuts

differentials: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy
per_call: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy

shortlist.label: COVID-19
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has severe bilateral pneumonia and positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2

shortlist.label: Optic neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed blurred vision, relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and impaired color and contrast vision in one eye

shortlist.label: Retinal vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Fluorescein Angiography showed fluorescein leakage from retinal venules inferotemporal to the macula

shortlist.label: Varicella-zoster virus retinitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has very weakly positive IgG for VZV, which could indicate past infection or reactivation

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus retinitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has very weakly positive IgG for CMV, which could indicate past infection or reactivation, and is a known cause of retinitis

raw.rationale: The patient's recent close contact with a fatal case, hospitalization for severe bilateral pneumonia, and positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2, along with the development of ocular symptoms, suggest a strong link between the patient's condition and COVID-19. The ocular findings, including relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and impaired color and contrast vision, can be associated with COVID-19-related ocular complications.

rejected.label: Optic neuritis
rejected.why: While optic neuritis could explain some of the patient's ocular symptoms, it does not account for the patient's systemic symptoms, such as severe bilateral pneumonia, and the positive SARS-CoV-2 test.

rejected.label: Retinal vasculitis
rejected.why: Retinal vasculitis is a possible complication of COVID-19, but as a standalone diagnosis, it does not fully explain the patient's respiratory symptoms and positive SARS-CoV-2 test.

rejected.label: Varicella-zoster virus retinitis
rejected.why: The patient's very weakly positive IgG for VZV does not strongly support this diagnosis, especially given the lack of other typical symptoms of varicella-zoster virus infection and the presence of a positive SARS-CoV-2 test.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus retinitis
rejected.why: The patient's very weakly positive IgG for CMV and the absence of other risk factors, such as immunocompromised status, make this diagnosis less likely, especially compared to the stronger evidence for COVID-19.

gold: Inflammation-induced ocular neuropathy associated with SARS-CoV-2–induced panuveitis
